The appellant - Lakhan Chadhar seeks suspension of sentence in his first attempt in I.A.
No.3077/2024 during the pendency of this appeal.

The appellant has been convicted and sentenced in the following manner :-

sentences.text: Initially, the mother of the prosecutrix lodged a missing report (Ex.P-9) on 30.03.2021.
On 31.03.2021, the prosecutrix was recovered and was handed over to her parents.

Documents i.e.
Panchnama Supurdagi vide Ex.P-3 and Ex.P-4 were prepared.
The appellant was arrested on 31.03.2021 and was tried in a Court of Law.

Learned counsel for appellant/applicant with reference to Ex.P-12 submitted that the age of the prosecutrix was not correctly determined in terms of Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 inasmuch as that the source of information had not submitted before the School Authority at the time when the prosecutrix was admitted in the School 2 CRA-1795-2024 on 30th June, 2011.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Narendra Kumar Yadav (PW-4) had specifically admitted in his statement that at the time of preparation of Dakhil Kharij Panji, there was no reference in respect of the documents on the basis of which the date of birth of the prosecutrix was recorded.

sentences.text: The prosecutrix while appearing as PW-1 specifically admitted that on the date of giving evidence on 17.11.2022, she was 20 years of age and her parents wrongly recorded her age in the school record.
The age recorded in her statement under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. was negated and it was asserted by her that her year of birth was 2002 and her parents wrongly recorded her year of birth as 2006.
She further admitted that she was in love with the applicant/appellant and also solemnized marriage.
They were blessed with a child.

During the course of the argument, learned counsel for appellant/applicant and learned counsel for the victim very candidly admitted that the prosecutrix is still living in her matrimonial house along with the parents of the appellant/applicant.

In view of the aforesaid position, the positive DNA profile would not advance the case of the prosecution as the prosecutrix specifically admitted that she was having love affair with the appellant/applicant and on account of that they entered into a matrimonial tie, resulting in birth of a child.
On the other hand, learned counsel for State opposed the prayer on the basis of findings recorded by the Court of Sessions.
Age of the prosecutrix would remain a debatable issue in the present appeal.

In view of the stand of the prosecutrix and other attaining circumstances of the case, we deem it appropriate to direct the release of appellant - Lakhan 3 CRA-1795-2024 Chadhar on bail b y suspending his remaining jail sentence, subject to his executing adequate bail bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand)
with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Chief Judicial Magistrate concerned with a further direction to appear before the trial Court concerned on 13.09.2024 and also on such other dates, as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard, during the pendency of this appeal.
The appellant shall deposit the fine amount and that would be the condition precedent for enlarging the appellant on bail and grant him suspension of sentence.
Nothing expressed hereinabove shall be construed to be an opinion on the merits of the case.
Accordingly, I.A. No.3077/2024 is allowed.
Certified copy as per rules.

(RAJ MOHAN SINGH) (DEVNARA  JUDGE J  DPS Lakhan Chadhar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158786338/
